T: Pines, white with frost, even in summer. The Frost Ward keeps its snow. Nobody knows how.
I: The ice house: thick stone, no windows, a door hung with bone charms.
5: THE ICE HOUSE. Pilgrims leave their boots outside, and letters by the door.
M: The drum tower. At dusk the curfew drums start here, and every drum in the city answers.
n: A tattered banner on the drum tower: not the fist and crown. A white wolf on blue. The old Kaldari standard.
F: The war-beast pens: war boars, war goats, and a war duck. The duck has its own pen. The duck needs its own pen.
A: A fur tent, in the old style from the wastes. Smoke from the top, smell of fish.
x: A fire of pine and old bones. Nobody here ever seems to feel the cold.
c: A lantern on a post, lit. Somebody keeps it burning.
^: North, back up to the bazaar.
J: A cocoon, half buried in snow.
The snow has settled on top of it in the shape of a little umbrella.

objects.name: Elder Skadi
lines: Sit, child. I'm the oldest Kaldari in the city. My people walked out of the wastes five hundred years ago.
'We walked south until the world ran out of winter.' That's what the first Elder said. So we brought a little winter with us.

answer: Ice to the edge of the sky. Wolves the size of houses. Nights a month long.
We were hard because the world was hard. Now the world's soft, and we're hard anyway. Habit.
When I was a girl the creed had three lines. The strong take. The weak give. The king takes most.
Then one winter, the king said he cast no shadow, and we added a fourth.
Kings don't usually need new lines, child. I've thought about that a long time.

questions.ask: Spare me your gran's stories, old woman.
answer: Nobody wanted them when she told them, either. Then she was gone, and everybody did.
Sit or go, child. The ice keeps them either way.

objects.name: Brug
lines: War boars! War goats! And Duchess. Duchess is the war duck. Don't look at Duchess.
Everybody's scared of the boars. Wrong. Fear the duck.

questions.ask: What's so bad about the duck?
answer: Duchess has fought in eleven wars. Nobody's sure which side. Nobody asked her.
She bit a king once. Not this one. Not yet. She's waiting, I think.

questions.ask: Duchess looks like dinner to me.
answer: * Somewhere in the pen, a duck stops quacking.
…Oh, you've done it now. She heard that.
Sleep with one eye open, friend. She sleeps with none.

objects.name: Frostwife Ylva
lines: Pilgrim. I've come to see the ice. The last ice from the wastes, kept five hundred years.
It's very cold. That's how you know it's real.

questions.ask: What do the pilgrims pray for?
answer: Cold. Winters long enough to remember who we were before the city.
Elder Skadi says the wastes were hard but honest. Nobody had a king. Only weather.

questions.ask: Came all this way for an ice cube?
answer: An ice cube that walked out of the wastes with our grandmothers. Five hundred years.
You came all this way to be rude to a pilgrim. Which of us made the better trip?

lines: THE DRUM TOWER. At dusk, one drum; then the city answers.
Carved small at the bottom, old: an open hand. Somebody's tried to scratch it off, and given up.

objects.name: Wynn
lines: Snow! In summer! Do you have ANY idea how beautiful that is?
Nobody knows why it snows here? Marvellous. I'll stand in it until I do.
Rain isn't bad weather, you know. It's the sky watering its garden. And snow is the sky tidying up.
* Wynn pops open a patched umbrella and wanders off into the snow, sniffing the air.
